name: Rincón Zapotec
confidence_why: Earl & Earl (2006/2011) state that stress falls on the first syllable of the root with monosyllabic prefixes and suffixes unstressed, and Martínez Pérez (2019), a native speaker describing eight Rincón communities, treats the root (base léxica) as the tonic syllable throughout, so the two first-hand descriptions agree on placement; only these two speak to stress at all (Alleman 1952 marks accents on entries but gives no rule), and their one disagreement is about whether the language also has lexical tone, not about where stress falls.

catalog_quote: [p. 359, §0.5 El acento y tono] "Toda palabra zapoteca de más de una sílaba tiene una sílaba acentuada. Las palabras aumentadas por afijos pueden tener dos o tres sílabas acentuadas, o aún cuatro. Aunque las palabras se distinguen por tonos en los demás dialectos del zapoteco, no hay tonos que distinguen las palabras del zapoteco del Rincón. El acento prosódico por lo general cae en la primera sílaba de la raíz. Si ésta no es la penúltima sílaba o si los sufijos cambia la posición de ésta a la que no es la penúltima se escribe el acento. Ejemplos: guba escoba guba / gubá sequía gubá / yutu + -do' calabacita yútudo' / zi'tu' + -lö de lejos zí'tu'lö / icja + -gaca + -bi' sus cabezas ícjagacabi'. Los prefijos y sufijos de una sílaba del verbo son átonos: ri- + lé'e + -da' veo rile'eda' ... chi- + gu- + dágu + -bi' ya comió chigudágubi'. Si la raíz del verbo empieza con una vocal, el prefijo de aspecto se amalgama con ésta para producir el acento en la primera sílaba. Ejemplos: ... g- + úl-la + -bi' cantará (fam) gúl-labi' ... Los prefijos y sufijos de una sílaba del sustantivo tampoco llevan acento." [p. 360] "Los prefijos y sufijos de dos sílabas llevan su propio acento en la primera sílaba. (No se escriben.) ... Los préstamos del español al zapoteco conservan el acento en la misma sílaba que en español. ... Dentro de la escritura en general solamente se escribe el acento que cae en la raíz de la palabra y no en los afijos, si ésta no está en la penúltima sílaba."

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the lexical root ('base léxica'): in the inherited *CV-ˈCV-CV word template a prefixal syllable is pretonic, the first syllable of the (historically disyllabic) root is tonic, and the root-final vowel is post-tonic. The post-tonic vowel is variably deleted or reduced to ɨ (/nisa/ → [nis] ~ [nisɨ] 'water'), so many surface words are monosyllabic with stress on that single root syllable; enclitics such as =ru are unstressed. Phonemic forms in the thesis mark stress accordingly, e.g. /u2-ˈse32ʤi2=ɾu2/ 'desatar', /ˈɡa2ti2=ɾu1/ 'morir', /ˈbe2.la1/ 'víbora', /ˈpa2ni/ 'rebozo'. No explicit 'el acento recae en..' sentence exists; the reading is inferred from the terminology, the template and the transcriptions.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (the IPA secondary-stress mark is only explained in the general phonetics chapter, p. 41).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Laryngealized (checked, rearticulated) vowels are restricted to the tonic syllable and weak creaky vowels to atonic syllables (p. 124); pretonic vowels are also reduced or lost in innovative communities and by male speakers (pp. 46, 158).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (prefix + root + enclitic); citation forms elicited from eight Rincón communities (Tanetze de Zaragoza, Juquila Vijanos, Otatitlán de Morelos, San Juan Yaeé, Santiago Camotlán, San Juan Yatzona, Santo Domingo Roayaga, Santa María Temaxcalapa). Tone (3 level, 6 contour) is contrastive and carried by the tonic vowel; the thesis is an orthography-oriented phonological description.
new_statements.identity_note: Martínez Pérez 2019 describes Didza Xidza = Rincón Zapotec [zar] (Smith Stark's 'Zapoteco del Rincón Norte' communities Tanetze de Zaragoza, Juquila Vijanos, Otatitlán de Morelos, San Juan Yaeé, Santiago Camotlán, San Juan Yatzona, Santo Domingo Roayaga, plus Santa María Temaxcalapa from his 'Rincón Sur' group); the author is a native speaker from Tanetze. Southern Rincón Zapotec (zsr, sout3034-type separate code) and Las Delicias Zapotec (zcd, split by ISO change request 2021-040) are excluded by Glottolog from rinc1236; Temaxcalapa data in the thesis may belong to the zsr group. Yateé (Didza Xhon, zty) is explicitly excluded by the author.

[...] Los prefijos y sufijos de una sílaba del verbo son átonos.
new_statements.translation: Every Zapotec word of more than one syllable has one stressed syllable. Words enlarged by affixes may have two or three stressed syllables, or even four. Although words are distinguished by tones in the other Zapotec dialects, there are no tones that distinguish words in Rincón Zapotec. Prosodic stress generally falls on the first syllable of the root. If that is not the penultimate syllable, or if suffixes move its position to one that is not the penult, the accent is written. [...] Monosyllabic prefixes and suffixes of the verb are unstressed.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog record for Rincón Zapotec has an empty rule; the existing statement (Martínez Pérez 2019) only implies stress on the 'base léxica' via pretónica/tónica/postónica positions. Earl's grammar sketch gives the explicit rule (first syllable of the root, affixes unstressed, disyllabic affixes with their own stress, loans keep Spanish stress) — compatible with the root-anchored picture and much more specific. It also asserts absence of tone, which disagrees with Martínez Pérez 2019's tone chapter (a tone question, not a stress-placement one).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the first syllable of the root; the orthography writes the accent only when that syllable is not the penult of the whole word (so the default surface position is often the penult, but the rule is root-anchored, not edge-counted). Monosyllabic prefixes and suffixes, on verbs and nouns alike, are unstressed; when a verb root begins with a vowel, the aspect prefix fuses with it and the stress lands on that first syllable (gázjabi', rásibi'). The grammar also states that Rincón Zapotec has no lexical tone, unlike other Zapotec varieties.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not called secondary, but: 'Los prefijos y sufijos de dos sílabas llevan su propio acento en la primera sílaba. (No se escriben.)' (p. 360) — disyllabic affixes (íla'-, búlu'-, -gáca, -tíqui'si) carry their own stress on their first syllable, so an affixed word can have two, three or four stressed syllables (example Gúla'guítjalentíqui'sigácabi'-ba' bö'cu' 'they always played with the dog', p. 360). The stressed vowel before a voiced consonant is lengthened (p. 360).
new_statements.exceptions: 'Los préstamos del español al zapoteco conservan el acento en la misma sílaba que en español' (p. 360): Spanish loans keep their Spanish stress (ximosoa', xirachua', rusumansa'-ba'). Vowel sequences: if stress is on the first of two vowels they count as two syllables (cúa, huóa), if on the second they count as one (béa', la'cua') (pp. 360-361).
new_statements.identity_note: Earl & Earl describe 'el zapoteco.. que se habla en el Rincón, en los distritos de Villa Alta e Ixtlán' and list about 25 mutually intelligible towns (Talea de Castro, Juquila Vijanos, Tanetze, Yaée, Yatzona, Camotlán, Yagavila, etc.) without naming a base dialect (Introducción p. iv). Alleman 1952 says only 'el dialecto del Rincón'. Martínez Pérez 2019 (existing statement) covers eight Rincón communities including Tanetze, Juquila Vijanos, Yaée, Yatzona, Camotlán. All are the same Glottolog languoid rinc1236.

readall_conflicts: On stress placement there is no disagreement: Earl (2011 draft grammar sketch, sec. 0.5) states stress on the first syllable of the root with unstressed monosyllabic affixes, and Martínez Pérez 2019 (the existing statement) treats the base léxica as the tonic position, so both are root-anchored. Alleman 1952 is silent. The one real disagreement is about tone, not stress: Earl writes 'no hay tonos que distinguen las palabras del zapoteco del Rincón', whereas Martínez Pérez 2019 devotes ch. 3 pp. 129-137 to tones across eight Rincón communities (and the 2014 INALI Tanetze slides held by the project show tone patterns). This should be recorded as a tone-status conflict between a 1950s-2011 SIL description and a 2019 native-speaker thesis, without changing the stress reading.
